measured.heard: The program sets N to 2 and switches on N. Case 2 has no break. The scenes that follow answer this question, one output line at a time. A switch jumps to the case label, whose value matches the controlling expression. With N equals 2, the matching label is case 2, which prints 2. A case label is only a label. It does not stop execution, so execution falls through into case 3, which prints 3. A break statement ends the smallest and closing switch or loop. Here that is the switch. After the switch ends, the program prints done. With break.c adds a break after case 1 and after case 2, so no case runs on into the next case. With N equals 2, with break.c prints only 2 from the switch, and then done. With W extra, GCC warns that the statements on line 7 and line 9 of fall through.c may fall through. And it gives with break.c no warning. Into break.c is fall through.c with case 3 cut down to a lone break. With N equals 2, it prints 2, falls into case 3, whose break ends the switch, and then prints done. For into break.c, GCC still warns at line 7, where case 1 falls into case 2, but says nothing at line 9, where case 2 falls into a case that only breaks. Apple clang with W extra gives no fall through warning for any of the 3 programs. A case label only marks where execution enters a switch. It never ends a case. In fall through.c, the break on line 12 is what ends the switch.
